mainTopic: Is the lottery (הגרלה) over the two goats of יום הכיפורים indispensable (מעכבא)? Testing the second version of the dispute between רבי ינאי and רבי יוחנן against ברייתות
overview: This amud asks whether the lottery (הגרלה) over the two goats of יום הכיפורים is מעכבא, meaning the service is invalid without it. It tests the second version (לישנא) of the dispute, where רבי ינאי holds that both רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה require the lottery. First, a ברייתא saying 'if he did not draw lots, it is valid' is fixed by reading it as 'placing' the lots (להניח). A second ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון, who elsewhere allows a replacement goat with no lottery at all. That seems to block the fix. The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון was replying to both possible meanings of the רבנן. Then a third ברייתא about the order of the פר and the שעיר seems to show that the lottery can come late, and so is not required. The גמרא defends רבי ינאי in two ways. The ברייתא may follow רבי שמעון, or it may follow רבי יהודה and only free the lottery's order, not the lottery itself. The amud ends by introducing a ברייתא, on the next amud, showing that רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון are consistent with these views.

steps.title: Under the second version, the ברייתא fits רבי יוחנן but not רבי ינאי
steps.stepSummary: Under the second לישנא, the ברייתא saying the lottery is not מעכבא fits רבי יוחנן (it follows רבי יהודה). It fits no one according to רבי ינאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the version where you said they disagree: it works well for the one who says the lottery is not indispensable, because this ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. But for the one who says it is indispensable, whose opinion is this ברייתא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא that says 'if he did not draw lots, it is valid.' It asks whose opinion that ברייתא can be according to רבי ינאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second לישנא, everyone agrees that רבי נחמיה holds the lottery is מעכבא. The argument is only about רבי יהודה. רבי יוחנן says that for רבי יהודה it is not מעכבא, so the ברייתא is simply רבי יהודה. רבי ינאי says it is מעכבא for both תנאים, so the ברייתא seems to have no author at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Version (of how a dispute was reported)
They disagree
Granted / it works well (sets up a contrast)
Indispensable; without it the service is invalid
Whose opinion is this?

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two לישנות. In this second version, the dispute between רבי ינאי and רבי יוחנן is only about רבי יהודה's view. Both agree that רבי נחמיה holds the lottery is מעכבא.

phrases.english: But according to that version in which you said they disagree,
granted, according to the one who said it is not indispensable,
whose is this? It is Rabbi Yehuda's,
but according to the one who said it is indispensable,
whose is this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-tests the earlier ברייתא, this time against the second version of the dispute
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי (second לישנא): the lottery is מעכבא according to both רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא rules the service valid without a lottery. If both תנאים hold the lottery is מעכבא, no one could have authored it.

steps.title: Change the wording: it is a מצוה to place the lots
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי's side changes the text of the ברייתא. It is not talking about drawing the lots but about placing them on the goats.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach the ברייתא as: 'It is a מצוה to place (the lots on the goats).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי ינאי by changing one word in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Drawing the lots out of the box (הגרלה) is מעכבא. Physically placing each lot onto a goat (הנחה) is only a מצוה. So 'if he did not, it is valid' refers to the placing, and the ברייתא no longer contradicts רבי ינאי.

keyTerms.meaning: Teach it as / read it as (a textual correction)
To place (the lots onto the goats)

phrases.english: Teach: it is a מצוה to place.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation (changing the wording of the ברייתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא said drawing the lots is not מעכבא
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא really means placing the lots is not מעכבא; drawing them still is

steps.title: A second ברייתא: no lottery and no confession, still valid
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא says: if he neither drew lots nor confessed, the service is valid. This again seems to go against רבי ינאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: it is a מצוה to draw the lots and to confess. If he did not draw lots and did not confess, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא to challenge רבי ינאי again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא also says the service is valid without the lottery, which goes against רבי ינאי. At first glance one could fix it the same way as before. The next step shows why that fix will not work here.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a source used as a proof or challenge)
To draw the lots
To confess (וידוי over the שעיר המשתלח)
Valid

phrases.english: Come and hear: it is a מצוה to draw lots and to confess.
If he did not draw lots and did not confess — it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New challenge against רבי ינאי after the first one was answered
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי: the lottery is מעכבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls the service valid without a lottery.

steps.title: The same fix fails because of רבי שמעון in the second half
steps.stepSummary: Suppose we change this ברייתא to 'placing' too. The סיפא quotes רבי שמעון saying: no lottery is valid, but no confession is invalid. That makes the fix a problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: here too, read it as 'to place' — then explain the סיפא: רבי שמעון says, if he did not draw lots it is valid; if he did not confess it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the easy answer of changing the word again. It points to the second half of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא brings רבי שמעון, who uses the same phrase 'לא הגריל.' To change the רישא, we would also have to change רבי שמעון's words. The next step shows that this creates a contradiction with רבי שמעון's known view.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (heads off a possible answer)
Say (look at) the latter clause
Invalid

phrases.english: And if you say: here too, it means 'to place,'
say the latter clause: Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִגְרִיל — כָּשֵׁר, לֹא הִתְוַדָּה — פָּסוּל.
phrases.english: If he did not draw lots — valid; if he did not confess — invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects ahead of time the idea of using the step 2 fix on the new ברייתא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Changing the second ברייתא to read 'to place'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The סיפא (רבי שמעון) uses the same wording, so the change would also have to apply there

steps.title: What does 'did not draw lots' mean in רבי שמעון's words?
steps.stepSummary: Suppose 'לא הגריל' means 'did not place.' Then רבי שמעון would hold that the actual drawing is מעכבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'he did not draw lots' mean? If you say it means 'he did not place,' that would show רבי שמעון holds drawing the lots is indispensable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what follows if we read רבי שמעון's words as 'did not place.' This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי שמעון's 'valid' only refers to placing, the implication is that the drawing itself is מעכבא for him. The גמרא will now test whether רבי שמעון really holds that.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (proposes a reading that will be tested)
By implication, it follows that
The lottery, drawing the lots

phrases.english: What is 'he did not draw lots'? If you say: he did not place,

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּלָל דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סָבַר הַגְרָלָה מְעַכְּבָא,
phrases.english: it follows that Rabbi Shimon holds drawing the lots is indispensable,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the step 4 problem is a real problem
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'לא הגריל' in רבי שמעון's statement
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Proposed reading: 'did not place.' This implies that, for רבי שמעון, הגרלה is מעכבא.

steps.title: רבי שמעון allows a replacement goat with no lottery at all
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון: if one goat died, its replacement is brought without a lottery. So for him the lottery is not מעכבא, and 'לא הגריל' must mean the real drawing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: if one of them died, he brings its partner without a lottery. These are the words of רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing that רבי שמעון does not consider the lottery מעכבא. This knocks out the 'placing' reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a replacement goat can serve with no lottery at all, then the drawing is not essential for רבי שמעון. So his 'לא הגריל, כשר' must mean the actual drawing, and it seems the רישא must also mean the actual drawing. That would make the 'להניח' fix fail. Step 7 answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא (introduces a contradicting source)
Its partner (the replacement goat)
Without a lottery

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, the lottery is not מעכבא, since a replacement goat needs none. So his own words 'לא הגריל, כשר' cannot mean 'did not place.' This seems to block the 'להניח' fix for the רישא too, which would leave the challenge against רבי ינאי (second לישנא) standing. The next step answers this.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the 'change the word' answer has limits. When the same wording appears in a clause whose author's view is known from elsewhere, it seems the text cannot be freely changed. Step 7 shows how the גמרא gets around this.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: if one of them died,
he brings its partner without a lottery,
these are the words of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disproves the implication drawn in step 5
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון does not hold הגרלה is מעכבא, so 'לא הגריל' means real drawing
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: if one goat died, the replacement is brought without a lottery (רבי שמעון)
steps.kashyaTarget: The proposed reading of רבי שמעון's 'לא הגריל' as 'לא הניח', and with it רבי ינאי's 'להניח' emendation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון rules that a replacement goat is brought without any lottery, so for him the drawing is not מעכבא. His 'לא הגריל, כשר' must therefore mean the real drawing, which contradicts the implication drawn in step 5.

steps.title: רבי שמעון was answering both possible meanings
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון did not know whether the רבנן meant the real drawing or only the placing. So he said: if you mean the real drawing, I argue with you on one point. If you mean placing, I argue with you on two points.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון did not know what the רבנן meant. This is what he told them: If by 'הגרלה' you mean the actual drawing, I disagree with you on one thing (the confession). If by 'הגרלה' you mean the placing, I disagree with you on two things (the drawing and the confession).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from Steps 4–6 and saves רבי ינאי's reading of the ברייתא. רבי שמעון's words were a two-sided answer, because he was not sure what the רבנן meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 proved that when רבי שמעון says 'הגרלה', he means the real drawing. That does not force the רבנן to mean the same thing. The רבנן can still mean 'placing', which is what רבי ינאי needs. רבי שמעון covered both options: on 'drawing' he would argue only about the confession, and on 'placing' he would also argue that the drawing is not מעכב.

keyTerms.meaning: The actual drawing of the lots from the box
Placing the drawn lots on the goats' heads
I disagree with you
On one point / on two points

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא no longer contradicts רבי ינאי. The רבנן's 'הגרלה' can mean placing, and רבי שמעון only spoke conditionally about what they might mean.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון is not changing his own opinion. For him the drawing is never מעכב. The 'one or two' only describes how many points he disagrees with the רבנן on, depending on what the רבנן meant.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon did not know
what the Sages were saying,
phrases.notes: Whether they meant drawing or placing

phrases.english: and this is what he said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אִי הַגְרָלָה — הַגְרָלָה מַמָּשׁ קָא אָמְרִיתוּ,
phrases.english: If by 'drawing' you mean the actual drawing,
I disagree with you on one point.
If the 'drawing' you mention means placing,
I disagree with you on two points.
phrases.notes: About the drawing and the confession

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לָא יָדַע מַאי קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty built in Steps 4–6 by separating רבי שמעון's meaning of 'הגרלה' from the רבנן's meaning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a speaker's intent: a conditional, two-sided reply
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי שמעון's 'הגרלה' means the real drawing, the רבנן's 'הגרלה' must mean the same, so the fix to 'placing' fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון spoke conditionally, so the רבנן may mean placing, and רבי ינאי stands.

steps.title: A new ברייתא about the order of the bull and the goat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: the פר holds back the שעיר, but the שעיר does not hold back the פר in the inner blood applications.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: The bull holds back the goat, but the goat does not hold back the bull, in the blood applications done inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge against רבי ינאי with 'תא שמע'. For now it is only quoting the ברייתא. The attack is built over the next steps and is stated in Step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכיפורים the services of the פר and the שעיר must go in a set order. The ברייתא says skipping a bull-service ruins a later goat-service. Skipping a goat-service does not ruin the bull-service. The גמרא will look for a case where that second rule makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: introduces a source used as proof or challenge
Holds back / disqualifies if missing or out of order
The bull of the כהן גדול
The goat, the חטאת of the people
The blood applications done inside the קודש הקדשים

phrases.english: Come and hear:
The bull holds back the goat,
and the goat does not hold back the bull
in the blood applications done inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: פַּר מְעַכֵּב אֶת הַשָּׂעִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the last challenge was answered, a fresh source is brought against רבי ינאי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's claim that everyone agrees the הגרלה is מעכב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא may show a case where a goat-related act (possibly the lottery) is not מעכב. That would go against רבי ינאי.

steps.title: What case is 'the goat does not hold back the bull'?
steps.stepSummary: The first half is easy to understand: a goat-service done before the bull-service counts for nothing. But what case fits the second half, that the goat does not hold back the bull?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that the bull holds back the goat: if he did the goat's service before the bull's, he did nothing at all. But 'the goat does not hold back the bull': what case is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first half of the ברייתא and then asks what case the second half describes. This question sets up the real challenge to רבי ינאי, which comes in Step 11 after one suggested case is ruled out in Step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the goat's blood was applied before the bull's, it does not count and must be redone after the bull. The reverse case is harder. Doing the bull before the goat is the normal order, so it is unclear what 'goat does not hold back bull' could mean. The גמרא will look for a goat-act whose absence leaves the bull valid, and that may turn out to be the lottery.

keyTerms.meaning: It is understandable / granted: 'this part is fine, but…'
He placed it earlier / did it first
He has done nothing at all
What is it? What case is meant?

steps.confusionAlert: 'Holds back' here is about order. Doing a later service before an earlier one makes it worthless. It does not mean one animal physically stops the other.

phrases.english: Granted, the bull holds back the goat:
for if he did the goat's service before the bull's,
he has done nothing at all.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שָׂעִיר אֵין מְעַכֵּב אֶת הַפָּר —
phrases.english: But 'the goat does not hold back the bull'
what case is that?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא quoted in Step 8, accepting its first half and asking about its second half.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case fits 'the goat does not hold back the bull', given that the bull normally comes first anyway?

steps.title: First suggested case is ruled out by the word 'statute'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the case is the פר's applications in the היכל done before the שעיר's applications inside. It rejects this, because the word חוקה is written about the inner services, so their order is required.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the case is where he did the bull's blood applications in the היכל before the goat's blood applications inside the קודש הקדשים, that cannot be. The word חוקה is written about these, so their order holds things back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first answer to the question from Step 9 and immediately rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The applications in the היכל come after the applications inside the קודש הקדשים. Doing the פר's היכל applications before the שעיר's inner applications breaks the order of the inner services. The word חוקה teaches that this order is מעכב, so the ברייתא could not call it valid.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
He did it earlier, out of order
Blood applications (sprinklings)
The Sanctuary, outside the קודש הקדשים, where blood is sprinkled toward the curtain
'Statute'. This word teaches that a service is required, including its order

steps.confusionAlert: 'בפנים' here means inside the קודש הקדשים, not just anywhere indoors. The היכל is a separate, outer room.

phrases.english: If you say that if he did earlier
the bull's applications in the Sanctuary
before the goat's applications inside,
'statute' is written about them.
phrases.notes: So the order is required and the ברייתא could not call this valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא דְּאִי אַקְדֵּים מַתָּנוֹת דְּפַר בַּהֵיכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first answer to the question in Step 9 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested case of the היכל applications done before the inner applications
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word חוקה makes the order of the inner services required, so the ברייתא could not call this case valid.

steps.title: The remaining case would show the lottery is not required
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא must mean that the פר's inner applications were done before the הגרלה. If the order of the lottery is not required, then the lottery itself is not required either. This is a challenge to רבי ינאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't the case where he did the bull's inner applications before the lottery? And since the order of the lottery does not hold things back, the lottery itself also does not hold things back!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the only case left, and it uses that case to challenge the view that the הגרלה is מעכבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the פר's service came before the הגרלה, and the ברייתא still calls it valid. So the lottery's place in the order is not required. The גמרא reasons that if its timing does not matter, the lottery itself must not matter either. This contradicts רבי ינאי, who holds that the הגרלה is מעכבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it that (pushes toward the remaining option)
The lottery that picks which goat is for ה׳ and which is for עזאזל
The order or sequence
Holds back; required, so without it the service is invalid
The thing itself, the essential act

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main attack in this section. It tests whether the lottery is a required part of יום הכיפורים.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it that he did earlier
the bull's applications inside
before the lottery.
And since the order does not hold back,
the lottery itself also does not hold back!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, דְּאַקְדֵּים מַתָּנוֹת דְּפַר בִּפְנִים מִקַּמֵּי הַגְרָלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the first case, the גמרא proposes the remaining case and draws a challenge from it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רבי ינאי that the הגרלה is מעכבא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls valid a case where the פר came before the lottery. So the lottery's order is not required, and therefore the lottery itself is not required.

steps.title: Another possible case that follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case could be the פר's applications on the מזבח done before the שעיר's applications in the היכל. This would follow רבי יהודה, who holds that white-garment services done outside are not מעכבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The case is where he did the bull's applications on the altar before the goat's applications in the Sanctuary. This follows רבי יהודה, who said that things done in white garments outside do not hold back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי ינאי by finding a different case that fits the ברייתא without involving the lottery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The applications on the מזבח happen outside the קודש הקדשים. רבי יהודה holds that white-garment services done outside are not מעכבי, so doing them out of order is still valid. In this case the ברייתא says nothing about the lottery.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden altar, where blood is applied after the היכל applications
The white garments the כהן גדול wears for the special יום הכיפורים services
Outside the קודש הקדשים
The תנא who holds that outer white-garment services are not required

phrases.english: No, where he did earlier
the bull's applications on the altar
before the goat's applications in the Sanctuary,
and it follows רבי יהודה, who said:
things done in white garments outside
do not hold back.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11 by offering a different case for the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting which case the ברייתא is describing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only possible case was the פר's applications done before the lottery.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case could be the מזבח applications done before the היכל applications, following רבי יהודה, so nothing is proven about the lottery.

steps.title: But the ברייתא is talking about the inner applications
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects this answer. The ברייתא explicitly says its rule applies to the inner applications, so it cannot be describing the applications on the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא teaches that it is speaking about the inner applications!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the answer from Step 12 by pointing back to the wording of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא in Step 8 said 'in the inner applications'. A case about the מזבח, which is outside, does not fit those words. So the challenge against רבי ינאי comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: But look (introduces a rebuttal)
That are inside the קודש הקדשים
It teaches (the ברייתא states)

steps.whatToRemember: The search for a case for 'the שעיר does not hold back the פר' has come back to the lottery case. That case suggests the הגרלה is not מעכבא, which challenges רבי ינאי. Steps 14 and 15 answer this.

phrases.english: But it teaches 'in the inner applications'!

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the ברייתא is describing the מזבח applications
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא explicitly limits its rule to the inner applications, and the מזבח applications are outside.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that the ברייתא teaches the lottery is not required. It explains that the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, so it is no problem for רבי ינאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: whose view is this ברייתא? It is רבי שמעון, who said the lottery is not required.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up the answer from step 12. Instead it says the ברייתא matches the view of רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא now agrees that the ברייתא is talking about the פר's inner applications done before the הגרלה. The ברייתא does imply that the lottery is not required. But that is only רבי שמעון's view. רבי ינאי claimed only that רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה hold the lottery is מעכבא, so a ברייתא following רבי שמעון does not contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals dropping the last answer and giving a new one.
Whose view is this?
The תנא who holds the lottery is not required
It does not hold back. In other words, it is not required for the service to count.

phrases.english: Rather: whose view is this?
phrases.notes: Drops the רבי יהודה answer from step 12.

phrases.english: It is רבי שמעון,
who said: the lottery is not required.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer from steps 12-13 with a new defense of רבי ינאי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא disproves רבי ינאי's rule that the lottery is required.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is רבי שמעון's view. רבי ינאי spoke only about רבי יהודה and רבי נחמיה, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: The ברייתא may still follow רבי יהודה: the order is optional, but the lottery is required
steps.stepSummary: This is a second answer. The ברייתא could be רבי יהודה. It only teaches that the lottery's order is not required, while the lottery itself still is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: really it is רבי יהודה. Granted, the order is not required, but the lottery itself is still required.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way to protect רבי ינאי. It rejects the reasoning from step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 argued that if the order of the lottery is optional, the lottery must be optional too. This answer cuts that link. The timing of the lottery can be flexible, while doing the lottery at all is still required.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say. It introduces a second answer.
Really, actually
Granted, even if
In its proper order
At least, nevertheless

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up two separate questions. One is whether the lottery must happen at the right time (its order). The other is whether it must happen at all. This answer says only the second one is required.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Actually, it is רבי יהודה,
and granted that doing it in order is not required —
the lottery itself is nevertheless required.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent answer to the challenge from step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If the order of the lottery is not required, the lottery itself is not required either.
steps.terutzMaskana: The order is not required, but the lottery itself is required, so רבי ינאי stands even according to רבי יהודה.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two defenses of רבי ינאי. (1) The ברייתא is רבי שמעון's view. (2) The ברייתא is רבי יהודה's view, and it only frees the order of the lottery, not the lottery itself.

steps.title: רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון are consistent: introducing a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that these two תנאים follow their usual reasoning. It introduces a ברייתא to show this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they follow their own reasoning, as it was taught in a ברייתא:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to quote a ברייתא showing that רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון hold these same views elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to show that the positions it just used are real and consistent. The ברייתא coming next will show the same disagreement between these two תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: And they follow their own reasoning (they are consistent with their views elsewhere)
As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: And they follow their own reasoning, as it was taught in a baraita:
phrases.notes: Setup. The ברייתא follows on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the positions given to רבי שמעון and רבי יהודה in steps 14-15.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds the lottery is not required, and רבי יהודה holds it is required
